narrative:
The model determined that you have a 52% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeds the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were your savings, the purpose of the loan, and the status of your checking account. Your savings of 1000 DM or more was the strongest factor and it worked in your favor, pulling the prediction toward approval. Having substantial savings is relatively rare among approved applicants and normally helps reduce risk in the bank's eyes.

Unfortunately, the purpose of the loan and your checking account status pushed strongly in the opposite direction. Requesting the loan to buy a new car worked against you; new-car loans are associated with higher risk compared with other purposes such as home-related financing that more approved applicants request. Similarly, having a checking account that typically sits between 0 and 200 DM signaled higher risk to the model. Most approved applicants either have no checking account or maintain clearly positive balances.

Taken together, the negative influence from the loan purpose and account status outweighed the positive signal from your savings, tipping the decision against approval.

You should focus on building a stronger checking-account history, consider a different loan purpose if possible, or explore smaller loan amounts. Reapplying once your financial profile shows more stability may improve your chances.
